transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Tom Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (CTO - Tethys), Samir Patel (ML Eng), Leah Kim (Product), Jordan (Procurement)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya with Redwood, this is Tom our solutions engineer. quick around the room?
[00:12] Priya: Hi Priya Rao, CTO at Tethys, we run a customer support automation platform, lots of long conversations, multilingual.
[00:18] Samir: Samir here, ML infra lead, we own model inference and cost.
[00:22] Leah: Leah, product, focused on latency and quality.
[00:26] Jordan: Jordan from procurement, tracking contracts.
[00:30] Tom: Cool, quick agenda: model selection, deployment options, security, and next steps.
[01:05] Maya: Priya, can you give context on current stack? what are you running today?
[01:12] Priya: We're mostly on a mix - inference in house on k8s with Triton for some models, and we also call out to a managed vendor for chat features. We're seeing cost spikes and maintenance burden. trying to decide if we go fully managed (hosted) or reserve dedicated capacity or fully private.
[02:10] Samir: Our main workload is multi-turn customer conversations. We need at least 8k context for summaries, some use-cases need up to 32k token windows for full conversation history. also multilingual: EN, ES, PT, FR, JA.
[02:45] Tom: OK, so context length is a driver. For models we support both 8k and 32k variants; open models like Llama-2 derivs, Mistral, Falcon, M** (note: some words clipped) have different perf and tokenization. do you have preferences on open models vs proprietary?
[03:15] Priya: We'd prefer open models for cost and control, but quality on non-English is a concern. Also tool-calling is important — our agents call internal DBs and external APIs. we need structured outputs.
[03:45] Leah: On the tool-calling piece, how do you ensure safe execution and auth?
[03:52] Tom: Redwood supports tool/function calling — we can pass structured schemas and restrict outputs. for private deployments you can run the control plane in your VPC and use native KMS for keys, so calls to internal APIs never leave your network if you want.
[04:30] Maya: let's dig into open model tradeoffs. Tom?
[04:35] Tom: Sure. Quick high level: Llama family variants are broadly good at chat and fine-tuning; Mistral variants are strong for instruction tasks and cost efficient; Falcon is strong in some long-context workloads but depends on quantization; newer families differ in tokenization for non-English. we often recommend a shortlist and run a benchmark with your prompts.
[05:10] Samir: How does Redwood pick kernels / runtime optimizations? we had issues with kv cache in our custom stack — slower at scale.
[05:18] Tom: Our serving runtime has attention optimizations and continuous batching. it picks kernels based on model arch and sequence length and manages KV cache. sometimes transcription or docs call this "K V cash" in notes, but it's KV cache. we also support quantized paths; there are tradeoffs for long context and accuracy.
[06:02] Priya: On the security side we need SOC 2 type II, optional ISO, SSO via SAML/Okta, audit logs, and ability to manage keys in our KMS/HSM. are these standard?
[06:18] Maya: Yes, Redwood Hosted is SOC2 and we provide audit logs, SSO. for Dedicated you get isolated pools and extra controls, and Private puts the control plane in your VPC or on-prem for full control and KMS integration.
[06:45] Jordan: Procurement question — what's the typical timeline to go from POC to dedicated reserved capacity contract?
[06:52] Maya: Typical is 6-12 weeks for a POC, then you can sign reserved capacity for Dedicated; timeline depends on procurement and SSO/security review.
[07:30] Leah: For multilingual tests, do you have prebuilt evals or do we supply our corpus?
[07:36] Tom: We can do both — Redwood Optimize has suggestions and prebuilt benchmarks, but we prefer you to supply a representative prompt set so we can measure real quality and cost.
[08:05] Priya: About function calling: we need the model to call our internal search and return structured JSON. any limitations on streaming vs function calls?
[08:15] Tom: Streaming is supported; function calling often uses the same token stream but we can enforce strict schema validation server-side and redact sensitive fields. for private deployments you can route those calls through internal endpoints.
[08:45] Samir: Can you run Canary rollouts between model versions? we want A/B on cost/latency/quality.
[08:52] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console supports canaries, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies if latency or quality regresses.
[09:20] Priya: Cost targets: we want to reduce per-session inference cost by ~30% compared to our current. is that realistic?
[09:28] Tom: With batching, caching and the right quantization/model choice it's feasible — we'll need to benchmark.
[10:00] Leah: What about context window expansion? moving some users to 32k tokens will increase cost. any tips?
[10:07] Tom: Use prefix caching for repeated system prompts, smart truncation and only keep necessary context. Redwood Optimize can suggest which prompts to cache and when to compress history.
[10:45] Samir: On the open model names, which exact checkpoints do you recommend for multilingual + tool-calling?
[10:52] Tom: For multilingual and tool-calling we often start with a robust 8k Llama-derivative or Mistral for instruction tuning, and evaluate 32k variants where available; if Java/Kanji heavy workloads we test tokenization. we also run a fallback to smaller models for cost-sensitive paths.
[11:40] Maya: I'm going to propose a pilot plan: 2-week benchmark using your top 100 prompts, evaluate 3 candidate models (Llama-deriv x8k, Mistral-instr x8k, Falcon/32k variant), measure latency, p95, token cost, and multilingual F1 on sampled responses. agree?
[12:05] Priya: yes that sounds good.
[12:12] Jordan: procurement will need a security pack and an NDA, can you share the SOC2 report and security questionnaire?
[12:20] Maya: yes I'll send SOC2, security package and our standard NDA.
[12:35] Tom: Quick technical note: tool-calling signed requests — we support signed tokens and short-lived credentials for functions so that model calls can only access allowed endpoints. this helps avoid leaking creds in prompts.
[13:05] Samir: latency: what's realistic p95 for a 4k prompt with streaming?
[13:12] Tom: On Dedicated it's typically sub-300ms p95 for generation steps depending on batch and model; hosted can vary by plan but we show performance profiles in the catalog. we'll capture exact numbers in the benchmark.
[14:00] Priya: Are there any limitations on model fine-tuning or instruction tuning in private mode?
[14:08] Tom: In Private you can fine-tune or use adapter stacks depending on your licensing for the model; we provide the tooling but some open checkpoints have license constraints. we'll flag license compatibility.
[14:45] Leah: For evaluation metrics, we care about hallucination rate and factuality on our KB. can Redwood integrate external evals?
[14:52] Tom: Yes, Redwood supports hooking in evaluation scripts and can run automatic regressions tied to prompt sets; we can alert on quality drift.
[15:30] Priya: Any notes on data retention? we need logs for debugging but can't retain PII beyond 30 days.
[15:38] Maya: We have retention controls — Hosted offers configurable retention windows and we can disable storage for PII-sensitive flows. Dedicated/Private give you stricter control.
[16:05] Samir: For the pilot we need test harness — do you have a runner we can use?
[16:12] Tom: We'll share a benchmark spreadsheet and a lightweight test harness (python) that hits the endpoints and records latency, tokens, and structured output checks.
[16:45] Priya: About pricing — how do you price Hosted vs Dedicated?
[16:50] Maya: Hosted is usage-based per-token/per-embedding with tiered rates. Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly commit) with predictable throughput and lower unit costs. Private has platform fees plus support. I'll include examples in the pricing doc.
[17:30] Jordan: Any legal friction points we should expect? export controls?
[17:36] Maya: Nothing unusual — we'll surface any model export/license constraints. for Private on-prem some legal review is simpler since data doesn't leave your premises.
[18:10] Tom: Quick PS on sampling — if you have few high-cost edge flows we can route them to cheaper models or use smaller contexts automatically.
[18:35] Samir: We also need SSO integration with Okta and group-based RBAC.
[18:42] Maya: Supported — we integrate SAML/Okta and can sync groups for RBAC.
[19:05] Leah: Are there rate limits or quotas for Hosted?
[19:12] Tom: Hosted has configurable quotas and rate limits per account and route; Dedicated gives you more predictable throughput.
[19:45] Priya: For multilingual quality testing, will you run a human eval or automated metric?
[19:53] Tom: We recommend a hybrid: automated metrics (BLEU/chrF, semantic similarity) plus a small human eval on sampled responses. Redwood offers tooling to manage that.
[20:30] Maya: ok let's recap and assign owners.
[20:35] Maya: Action items: I'll send pricing and SOC2, Tom will send benchmark harness, Priya will provide prompt set, Jordan will confirm procurement timeline.
[21:02] Priya: sounds good.
[21:10] Jordan: we'll aim to review docs by Monday.
[21:30] Tom: one more technical note — model variants for 32k are still maturing; we'll include a caveat on latency and sometimes tokenization oddities in non-latin scripts.
[22:05] Samir: that's fine, we'll evaluate.
[22:25] Leah: timeline: pilot next week? feasible?
[22:30] Maya: We can kick off the benchmark as soon as you share prompts and we provision test keys — target start 2026-04-20.
[23:00] Priya: ok will aim for that.
[23:20] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and the benchmark link.
[23:35] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcription: some product names or acronyms may be slightly off; speaker labels may have minor attribution errors.
